answer: The summit test I would run is Allotment tenancy agreement with council rent records: a tenancy held with one council across years, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. What makes this stick is that a tenancy held with one council across years cannot be faked in bulk — each proof is independent, and the knoll of independence is that one compromised proof endangers no other account. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the saffron of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
